q-72854:
First, notice that the $1$st and the $3$rd rows are the same in both matrices. The only row that has changed is the $2$nd row. 

By considering the given row operations that modify the $2$nd row, we notice that

$$
\begin{aligned}X & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 \\ -4 & -1 & 1 \\ 2 & 1 & 6\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+4\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 3 & 9 \\ 2 & 1 & 6\end{aligned}] \\  & =W.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the required row operation is

$$
{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+4{R}_{1}.
$$

q-72860:
Of the given options, we consider the row operation 

$$
{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-3{R}_{1}={R}_{3}+(-3)\cdot {R}_{1}
$$

Applying the above row operation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}S & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 \\ 3 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 3\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-3)\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 \\ 3 & 2 & 1 \\ -2 & 4 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the required row operation is 

$$
{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-3)\cdot {R}_{1}
$$

or simply

$$
{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-3{R}_{1}.
$$

q-130285:
Of the given options, we consider the row operation 

$$
{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{1}.
$$

Applying the above row operation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}6 & 2 & 4 \\ -9 & 1 & -5 \\ 8 & 4 & 0\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-2)\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}6 & 2 & 4 \\ -9 & 1 & -5 \\ -4 & 0 & -8\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the required row operation is

$$
{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{1}.
$$

q-81203:
The complement of $A,$ denoted $\overset{―}{A},$ consists of every element in the universal set $U$ that is not in the set $A.$

The elements of $U$ that are not in $A$ are $1,$ $3,$ $5,$ $7,$ and $9.$

Therefore, the complement of $A$ is

$$
\overset{―}{A}={1,3,5,7,9}.
$$

q-105179:
The complement of $B,$ denoted $\overset{―}{B},$ consists of every element in the universal set $U$ that is not in the set $B.$

The elements of $U$ that are not in $B$ are $2,$ $6,$ $10,$ $14,$ and $18.$

Therefore, the complement of $B$ is

$$
\overset{―}{B}={2,6,10,14,18}.
$$

q-81205:
The complement of $A,$ denoted $\overset{―}{A},$ consists of every element in the universal set $U$ that is not in the set $A.$

The universal set $U$ consists of the even integers $-20$ through $20,$ while the set $A$ consists of the multiples of $4$ from $-20$ through $20.$

So, the only elements of $U$ that are not in $A$ are the even integers from $-18$ through $18$ that are not multiples of $4.$

Therefore, the complement of $A$ is

$$
\overset{―}{A}={-18,-14,-10,-6,-2,2,6,10,14,18}.
$$

q-105188:
The complement of $Y,$ denoted $\overset{―}{Y},$ consists of every element in the universal set $U$ that is not in the set $Y.$

The universal set $U$ consists of the letters $a$ through $z,$ while the set $Y$ consists of the letters $a$ through $j.$

So, the only elements of $U$ that are not in $Y$ are the letters $k$ through $z.$

Therefore, the complement of $Y$ is

$$
\overset{―}{Y}={k,l,m,…,z}.
$$

q-73145:
The first non-zero entry of each row (from left to right) is the leading entry. 

Therefore, the leading entries of the $1$st and $4$th rows of $A$ are $1$ and $-3$, respectively.

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 1 & 3 \\ 4 & 3 & 0 & 0 \\ -2 & 0 & -1 & 8 \\ 0 & -3 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

So, the answer is $1+(-3)=-2.$

q-73148:
The first non-zero entry of each row (from left to right) is the leading entry. 

Therefore, the leading entries of the $1$st, $2$nd, and $3$rd rows of $A$ are $-7$, $5$, and $3$, respectively.

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}0 & -7 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 5 & 6 \\ 3 & 0 & 2 & -1 \\ -1 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

So, the answer is $-7+5+3=1.$

q-72491:
Remember that a matrix is in row echelon form if it satisfies the following conditions:

I. All the zero rows (rows with only zeros), if any, are placed at the *bottom* of the matrix.

II. Each leading entry of a row is in a column *to the right* of the leading entry of the row above it.

With that in mind, let's look at each matrix in turn.

- The matrix $A$ is not in row echelon form since the leading entry ${a}_{43}\ne 0$ (condition II is violated). 

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}6 & 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 6 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

- The matrix $B$ is in row echelon form (both conditions are satisfied).

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 5 & 1 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}]
$$

- The matrix $C$ is not in row echelon form since the leading entry ${c}_{32}\ne 0$ (condition II is violated). 

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}5 & 5 & 3 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 5 & 3 \\ 0 & 2 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & -7 & 4\end{aligned}]
$$

Therefore, only $A$ and $C$ are **not** in row echelon form.

q-129213:
Remember that a matrix is in row echelon form if it satisfies the following conditions:

I. All the zero rows (rows with only zeros), if any, are placed at the *bottom* of the matrix.

II. Each leading entry of a row is in a column *to the right* of the leading entry of the row above it.

With that in mind, let's look at each matrix in turn.

- The matrix $A$ is in row echelon form (both conditions are satisfied).

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 5 & 0 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

- The matrix $B$ is in row echelon form (both conditions are satisfied).

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 & 2 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 7\end{aligned}]
$$

- The matrix $C$ is not in row echelon form since the second row contains only zeros and it is not at the bottom of the matrix (condition I is violated).

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 5 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -9\end{aligned}]
$$

Therefore, only $A$ and $B$ are in row echelon form.

q-72575:
Remember that an augmented matrix is in row echelon form if its coefficient matrix satisfies the following conditions:

I. All the zero rows (rows with only zeros), if any, are placed at the *bottom* of the matrix.

II. Each leading entry of a row is in a column *to the right* of the leading entry of the row above it.

With that in mind, let's look at each matrix in turn.

- The matrix $A$ is in row echelon form (both conditions are satisfied).

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -3 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}]
$$

- The matrix $B$ is not in row echelon form since ${b}_{22}\ne 0$ (condition II is violated).

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 4 & 9 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 & 1 \\ 2 & 1 & 5 & 5\end{aligned}]
$$

- The matrix $C$ is in row echelon form (both conditions are satisfied).

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 0 & 0 & -1 & 6 \\ 0 & -2 & 0 & 0 & 2 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & -3 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Therefore, only $B$ is **not** in row echelon form.

q-42008:
Notice that by replacing ${a}_{21}$ and ${a}_{43}$ with $0$, we get a matrix in row echelon form:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 4 & 7 \\ 2 & 4 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 5 & 6 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 3\end{aligned}]\,⟶\,[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 4 & 7 \\ 0 & 4 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 5 & 6 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

The other options will not give us a matrix in row echelon form.
